title: Curation worklist
description: names/work/curate.json: the rows of names/places.csv the last `frasch match` left for a human, with their candidates. `frasch curate export` writes it (frasch/curate.py), the curation view (web `?curate`, web/src/dev/curateWorklist.ts) reads it through the Vite dev server. It carries every rule of the name list the view needs, so that the browser reads no cell of places.csv itself.

bbox.description: North Frisia, which the view's lookups search in: lon_min, lat_min, lon_max, lat_max.

kind_order.description: The kinds in the order the view offers them and the rows come in: those a human decides quickly first.

polygon_kinds.description: The kinds whose local reference can be labelled with a square of an area (`polygon_km2`) instead of a node.

class_keys.description: The OSM tags that say what kind of thing an object is, the most telling first (frasch/osmtags.py): a candidate's `class` is the value of the first of them it has, and the view sums a lookup result up by them.

settlement_places.description: The `place` values of a settlement: a candidate whose `class` is one of them is a place where people live.

results.description: The results a row can have, for the view's filter.

rows.description: By kind in `kind_order`, each kind in places.csv order.

result.description: What the matcher made of a row it left for review: several plausible OSM objects, or none.

row.description: One row of places.csv, what the matcher said about it, its candidates and where its hint points.

id.description: The places.csv row's `id`: what the decisions are keyed on.

line.description: Its line in places.csv at export time (header = 1); shown, never used to find the row.

name.description: The Frisian name `frasch match` worked with: the primary name of the first name column that has one.

names.description: Every non-empty Frisian name column, raw cell text, keyed by column name.

name_de.description: The primary German name: the first variant of `de`, its remarks stripped. Empty when the row has none.

name_da.description: The primary Danish name, read from `da` like `name_de`.

de.description: The German cell, raw: every variant with its remarks.

why.description: Why the matcher gave up (the `note` of work/matches.csv).

hint_point.description: Where the first place of the hint lies: lon, lat, radius in km. null for a row without a hint, or with one nothing resolves.

candidates.description: The OSM objects the matcher considered, best first.

candidate.description: One OSM object the matcher considered for a row.

name.description: Its OSM name, cut to 40 characters.

class.description: What it is, in one word: the value of its `place` tag, else of the next tag that says (`natural`, `boundary`, ...), else `-`.

km.description: Its distance from the centre of North Frisia in km, as `frasch match` computed it. null for an object without a position.

lon.description: null when work/candidates.jsonl no longer has the object (rebuilt since the match), or has no position for it.

tags.description: The tags that say what kind of thing it is, `place=hamlet;boundary=administrative`. Empty when work/candidates.jsonl no longer has the object.

in_sh.description: Whether it is in the Schleswig-Holstein extract the tiles are built from: only such an object can carry an injected name.

wikidata.description: The object's `wikidata` tag, raw (OSM sometimes lists several ids); left out when it has none.
